# Mesh

Namespace `Nfty.Model` in assembly `Nfty.Model`.

```csharp
public sealed class Mesh
```

A triangle mesh: what `Riser` builds, what the writers serialize, and what the step-6 preview rasterizes. Immutable — every array is copied in and exposed read-only — and every derived value is computed in the constructor, never lazily (mixel's D7), so one mesh may be read from many threads.

## Remarks

**Vertex rule.** A mesh straight from `Riser` shares a vertex only between the two triangles of its own quad: four vertices and six indices per quad, so [`Mesh.VertexCount`](Nfty.Model.Mesh.md#p-vertexcount) is twice [`Mesh.TriangleCount`](Nfty.Model.Mesh.md#p-trianglecount). That is the fast build the Rise page repeats per stroke. [`Mesh.Compact()`](Nfty.Model.Mesh.md#m-compact) merges bit-identical (position, normal, uv) vertices for the written file.

Coordinates follow glTF: +Y up, +Z toward the viewer. Texture coordinates put (0,0) at the image's top-left, so v grows downward with the image row.

## Constructors

### Mesh(float\[], float\[], float\[], uint\[], int, int) { #m-ctor-system-single-system-single-system-single-system-4bbee3 }

```csharp
public Mesh(float[] positions, float[] normals, float[] texCoords, uint[] indices, int textureWidth, int textureHeight);
```

Builds a mesh, copying every array.

**Parameters**

- `positions` (`float[]`) - xyz per vertex.
- `normals` (`float[]`) - One xyz unit normal per vertex.
- `texCoords` (`float[]`) - One uv per vertex.
- `indices` (`uint[]`) - Three vertex indices per triangle, counter-clockwise seen from outside.
- `textureWidth` (`int`) - Width of the image the UVs address.
- `textureHeight` (`int`) - Height of the image the UVs address.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException` - The arrays disagree about the vertex count, an index names no vertex, or a position is not finite.

## Methods

### Compact() { #m-compact }

```csharp
public Mesh Compact();
```

A copy with every set of bit-identical (position, normal, uv) vertices merged into one, no epsilon. Vertices are numbered in first-seen order, so the same mesh always compacts to the same bytes; triangle count, winding and bounds are unchanged. It costs a hash pass, which is why the writers pay it and the live preview does not.

**Returns.** The compacted mesh; this mesh itself when nothing merges.
